rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Snell's law is $n_1\sin\theta_1 = n_2\sin\theta_2$ with no mention of which is larger. ✅ Snell's law shows that when $n_2 > n_1$: $\sin\theta_2 < \sin\theta_1$, so $r < i$ (ray bends toward normal). When $n_2 < n_1$: $r > i$ (ray bends away from normal). The direction of bending is determined by the relative densities.  ·  ❌ The refractive index $n$ can be less than 1. ✅ For real materials at optical frequencies, $n > 1$ because $v < c$. In some special cases (metamaterials at microwave frequencies), engineered materials can have $n < 1$, but this doesn't apply to standard optical media.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ A larger refractive index means faster light in that medium. ✅ LARGER refractive index means SLOWER light. The relationship is $n = c/v$: larger $n$ means smaller $v$. Diamond ($n \approx 2.4$) is optically the fastest glass.  ·  ❌ The critical angle formula is $\sin\theta_c = \frac{n_1}{n_2}$. ✅ The correct formula is $\sin\theta_c = \frac{n_2}{n_1}$ where $n_1 > n_2$ (denser to rarer). Using $\frac{n_1}{n_2} \approx \frac{1.52}{1} = 1.52 > 1$ would give $\sin\theta_c > 1$, which is impossible for real angles.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Snell's law was first quantitatively formulated by Willebrord Snellius (Snell) in 1621, though the law was known to Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) in the 11th century. Fermat's principle of least time provides the variational derivation of Snell's law.  ·  The refractive index varies with wavelength (dispersion) because the polarization response of matter to electric fields depends on frequency. This is fundamental to fiber optics, laser technology, and understanding celestial atmospherics.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Snell's law (First law of refraction):** When light passes obliquely from one medium to another, $\frac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant} = \frac{n_2}{n_1}$, where $i$ is the angle of incidence, $r$ is the angle of refraction, and $n_1$, $n_2$ are the refractive indices of the first and second media respectively. This law is the basis of all refraction phenomena.  ·  **Refractive index definition:** $n = \frac{c}{v}$, where $c = 3.00 \times 10^8\,\text{m/s}$ is the speed of light in vacuum and $v$ is its speed in the medium. Since $v < c$ always, $n > 1$ for all real materials. Higher $n$ means light travels slower in that medium.  ·  **Relative refractive index:** $n_{21} = \frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{v_1}{v_2}$. This is the refractive index of medium 2 as seen from medium 1. When light enters a denser medium ($n_2 > n_1$), it bends TOWARD the normal. When entering a rarer medium, it bends AWAY from the normal.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Dispersion only happens with prisms. ✅ Dispersion occurs at EVERY refracting surface. Prisms make dispersion visible because they have large apex angles, but rainbows form from millions of tiny atmospheric droplets acting as prisms.  ·  ❌ The angle of refraction is always greater than the angle of incidence. ✅ Refraction angle is SMALLER than incidence angle when entering denser medium, and LARGER when entering rarer medium. The ray bends toward normal in denser medium, away in rarer medium.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Laws of refraction: refractive index
